import sys
from datetime import date

        lines = f.readlines()

    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        match = RELEASE_HEADER_PATTERN.match(line)

        lines[i] = f"## {version} ({today})\n"
        print(f"Added date: {version} ({today})")

        with open(RELEASE_NOTES_FILE, "w") as f:
            f.writelines(lines)
        sys.exit(0)

    print("No release header found")
    sys.exit(1)

python3 - <<'PY'
import re
import sys
from datetime import date

SUPPORTED_LANGS = {
    "de", "en", "es", "fr", "ja", "ko", "pt", "ru", "tr", "uk", "zh", "zh-hant",
}
RELEASE_HEADER_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^## (\d+\.\d+\.\d+)\s*(\\(.*\\))?\s*$")

def main() -> None:
    for lang in SUPPORTED_LANGS:
        release_notes_file = f"docs/{lang}/docs/release-notes.md"
        try:
            with open(release_notes_file, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                lines = f.readlines()
        except FileNotFoundError:
            print(f"Skipping {lang}: {release_notes_file} not found.")
            continue

        for i, line in enumerate(lines):
            match = RELEASE_HEADER_PATTERN.match(line)
            if not match:
                continue

            version = match.group(1)
            date_part = match.group(2)

            if date_part:
                print(f"Latest release {version} in {lang} already has a date: {date_part}")
                continue

            today = date.today().isoformat()
            lines[i] = f"## {version} ({today})\\n"
            print(f"Added date: {version} ({today}) to {lang}")

            with open(release_notes_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.writelines(lines)
            sys.exit(0) # Exit after first successful update

    print("No release header found in any supported language release notes.")
    sys.exit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
